question_text: A 58-year-old woman with a history of Riedel's thyroiditis. He has abdominal pain, weight loss and obstructive jaundice. In view of the radiological suspicion of pancreatic carcinoma, a cephalic duodenopancreatectomy is performed. In the anatomopathological study we did not find a carcinoma, but abundant inflammatory cells with a tendency to surround ducts, marked fibrosis, obliterating phlebitis and more than 50 IgG4 + plasma cells per high-power field. Which is the diagnosis?
